title: Reading a certificate
summary: Walk through every field of a real certificate and learn which ones matter when something breaks.

steps.title: A certificate, decoded
body: This is what `openssl x509 -in shop.pem -noout -text` prints. Every certificate on the web has this shape.
Issuer: C=US, O=Example Trust, CN=Example Issuing CA 2
Read it top to bottom: **who issued it** (Issuer), **when it is valid** (Validity), **who it is for** (Subject and the
Subject Alternative Name), **the key**, then **extensions** that limit what it may be used for. The issuer's signature comes last
> **Tip:** On Windows, `certutil -dump shop.cer` prints the same information, and double-clicking a `.cer` opens the viewer.

steps.prompt: Using the certificate above: which hostnames is it valid for? (Select all that apply.)
steps.explain: Hostnames come from the **Subject Alternative Name** (SAN) list. Only names listed there match. `api.shop.example` is not listed and there is no wildcard.

steps.prompt: Match each field to the question it answers.
pairs: Which certificate is this, among all the issuer has signed?
Which hostnames or IPs does it cover?
Proof the issuer approved the contents

steps.title: Extensions: what the certificate is allowed to do
body: Version 3 certificates carry **extensions**. Four of them cause most real-world trouble:
| **Basic Constraints** | Is this a CA, i.e. may it sign other certificates? | `CA:FALSE` on a leaf, `CA:TRUE` on a CA |
| **Key Usage** | Low-level operations the key may do | `Digital Signature` (leaf), `Certificate Sign, CRL Sign` (CA) |
| **Extended Key Usage** (EKU) | Purposes | `TLS Web Server Authentication` (serverAuth), `TLS Web Client Authentication` (clientAuth) |
| **Subject / Authority Key Identifier** | IDs of this cert's key and of the issuer's key | used to link a cert to its issuer |
**critical** means "if you don't understand this extension, reject the certificate".
The **thumbprint** (Windows) or **fingerprint** (openssl) is *not* a field. It is a SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash of the whole certificate,
computed by whoever is looking at it. It is a handy unique ID: `Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My\<thumbprint>`.

steps.prompt: Would you expect this on a **leaf** (a website's certificate) or on a **CA** certificate?
Which statement about the thumbprint is true?
options: It is a hash of the whole certificate, so it changes when the certificate is renewed, even with the same key
It is stored inside the certificate by the CA
It is secret and should not be logged
It stays the same across renewals because the subject name is the same
steps.explain: Renewal produces new bytes (new serial, new dates), so a new thumbprint. Config that pins a thumbprint (IIS bindings, `appsettings.json`) must be updated on every renewal, a classic outage cause.

steps.prompt: Reading fields in .NET. The validity runs from 2030-01-01 to 2031-01-01 UTC. What does this print?
code: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=shop.example", key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
steps.explain: `NotAfter` comes back in local time, so convert to UTC before printing. Basic Constraints says not a CA, and we marked it critical. `Thumbprint` is a SHA-1 hash in hex: 20 bytes, 40 characters.

steps.title: Inspect a certificate
prompt: Write two methods that read a certificate:
- `bool IsCa(X509Certificate2 cert)`: true only when a Basic Constraints extension exists and says it is a CA.
- `List<string> DnsNames(X509Certificate2 cert)`: the DNS names in the Subject Alternative Name extension, in order.
Return an empty list when there is no SAN.
The namespaces are imported; **Run checks** builds test certificates for you.
solution: return san == null ? new List<string>() : san.EnumerateDnsNames().ToList();
hints: `FirstOrDefault()` returns null when the extension is missing.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Test Root", null, true);

using var dojoBare = new CertificateRequest("CN=bare", dojoKey, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256).CreateSelfSigned(new DateTimeOffset(2030, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero), new DateTimeOffset(2031, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
Dojo.Eq("IsCa on a cert with no Basic Constraints is false", false, IsCa(dojoBare));
Dojo.Eq("DnsNames on a cert with no SAN is empty", new List<string>(), DnsNames(dojoBare));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
